# Solver parity corpus

`WeightedSquaredErrorScorer` deliberately mirrors the Elixir
`ColorMatching.WeightedSquaredError` solver so the macOS client and the
`color_matching` server always agree on palette-color selection. Parity is
**enforced**, not assumed: a golden-vector corpus generated by the Elixir
solver is committed to this repository and replayed by tests.

## Where the corpus lives

| | Path |
| --- | --- |
| This repo (committed fixture) | `ColorComposerCore/Tests/Fixtures/parity/v1/corpus.json` |
| Upstream source of truth | [`color_matching`](https://github.com/viamin/color_matching) → `priv/parity/v1/corpus.json` |

Provenance of the currently committed copy:

- Upstream commit: `47057afd58f7d46b4d4b740ca7d2d08947774471` (`main`, 2026-10-31)
- SHA-256: `7b7b4d904ff369e1f5be0ec3a994d96cc996056e856d86a2b764b83c050f8604`
- Generated by `mix parity.generate` (deterministic; upstream
  `mix parity.generate --check` guards against drift on the server side)

Note: the issue references upstream PRs viamin/color_matching#110 (OpenAPI
spec) and #111 (parity corpus). Neither PR was open at the time this fixture
was captured; the corpus content is already on `main` at the commit above.
The pinned `color_matching` gitlink in this repo (`61d81f2…`) predates the
corpus, so the fixture was fetched from `main` directly.

## How to refresh

1. In a checkout of `viamin/color_matching`, run `mix parity.generate` and
   commit the result upstream (or pull the latest `main`).
2. Copy `priv/parity/v1/corpus.json` verbatim over
   `ColorComposerCore/Tests/Fixtures/parity/v1/corpus.json` in this repo.
3. Run `cd ColorComposerCore && swift test --filter SolverParityCorpusTests`.

A corpus bump is a **review event**: the test asserts `algorithm_version == 1`
and fails loudly on an unknown version, so an upstream algorithm change cannot
silently invalidate parity. When diffing a refreshed corpus, review any
changed `expected` blocks before merging — changed scores mean the two
implementations disagree and one of them must change.

## What the parity test asserts

`ColorComposerCore/Tests/ColorComposerCoreTests/SolverParityCorpusTests.swift`
loads the fixture and, for every scenario:

- each candidate's score matches **exactly** (bit-for-bit `Double` equality —
  corpus values are dyadic rationals, and both sides accumulate
  `weight * (candidate − target)²` in canonical channel order), or is
  `excluded` exactly where the corpus says so;
- the selection (lowest score, **earliest index wins ties**) matches
  `selected_index`, `selected_hex_color`, and `error`;
- the tie set matches `tied_indices` and `tie_broke`;
- the same scenario replayed through `CompositionSolver`'s production fast
  path (1×1 grids) produces the identical selection, per-cell error, and
  excluded-candidate count.

Corpus v1 covers 12 scenarios: `distinct-errors`, four tie cases
(`tie-symmetric-around-target`, `tie-duplicate-vectors`, `tie-three-way-on-lps`,
`mixed-large-palette`), missing-measurement exclusions
(`missing-candidate-excluded`, `missing-target-excluded`, `all-excluded`),
zero-weight-channel tolerance (`zero-weight-channel-missing`),
single-channel (`single-channel-lps`), exact zero-error
(`exact-match-zero-error`), unknown light-source weights
(`unknown-weight-ignored`), and an 8-color mixed palette.

## Parity findings (v1 corpus)

- **Ties** — exact-score ties are real and common in the corpus; the winner is
  always the earliest palette index. The Swift solver's strict
  `score < bestScore` comparison reproduces this; any `<=` would flip
  tie cases to the *latest* index and fail the corpus.
- **Exclusions** — a candidate missing a measurement on any positive-weight
  channel is *excluded* (never treated as zero brightness). When the *target*
  is missing a positive-weight channel, every candidate is excluded and no
  selection exists (the solver records `nil` for the cell). Such a target
  cannot be expressed through grid-based solving, so that scenario is
  asserted at the scorer level only.
- **Weight handling** — a channel with weight `0` (present but zero) neither
  excludes nor contributes; weight keys for light sources the client does not
  model (e.g. `ultraviolet`) are ignored entirely.
- **Result** — the Swift scorer matches all 12 scenarios exactly: scores,
  exclusions, selections, tie sets, and errors. No parity defects were found.
